en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Jar.
5. The Question on the Ingredients of Antidotes “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two ingredients of an antidote must be taken,’ which are those two ingredients that must be taken?
“Just as, Great King, worms do not take hold within an antidote;”
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga should not allow mental defilements to take root.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the antidote that must be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the antidote repels all poisons—whether encountered through being bitten, touched, seen, eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted.
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, must repel all the poison of lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, and wrong view.
This, Great King, is the second factor of the antidote that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above gods:
‘By a yogi who wishes to see the true nature of conditioned phenomena,
one must proceed as if with an antidote.’
“In destroying the poison of the defilements.
Thus ends the fifth question on the ingredients of medicine.
